conventions.convention: Complex classical varieties are separated and quasi-compact, with finite affine-model covers; their topological uses carry the analytic topology obtained from Euclidean affine charts. Smoothness means regularity of the algebraic local ring.

A finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification has nonempty connected locally closed smooth strata with reduced induced algebraic structures; each analytic closure is a union of strata. The definition supplies no existence or common-refinement theorem.

Finite-rank local constancy means local isomorphism to a finite power of the constant sheaf, including rank zero. Rank is quantified locally; neither global triviality nor a fundamental-groupoid comparison is assumed.

D_c^b(X;k) is a full subcategory of the bounded derived category, defined by cohomology sheaves locally constant of finite rank on one witnessing finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification. Shifts satisfy H^j(A[m]) = H^{j+m}(A).

Injective-model comparisons assume AC and use k-linear injectives. Cone closure is proved for a fixed stratification, or for inputs sharing one common witnessing stratification; arbitrary k-injectives are not asserted injective as abelian sheaves.
Poset diagrams are covariant, with arrows p → q when p ≤ q; h counts strict inequalities. Bar resolutions have cochain degree −n. Empty-poset sections and derived Hom models are zero.
The singular/sheaf comparison assumes AC and a metric space with a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets. The cohomology-of-a-point consequence additionally requires nonempty contractibility.

load_bearing.statement: D_c^b(X;k) is the full subcategory of D^b(Sh_k(X)) consisting of complexes with bounded cohomology whose cohomology sheaves restrict to finite-rank locally constant sheaves on one witnessing finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification.

The analytic topology is obtained by gluing Euclidean affine-model topologies; regular maps are continuous. A finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification decomposes X into nonempty connected locally closed smooth reduced algebraic strata, each closure being a union of strata.
A sheaf F of k-vector spaces is locally constant of finite rank if every point has an open neighbourhood U on which F is isomorphic to k_U^n for an integer n ≥ 0.

Under AC, Sh_k(X) is a locally small Grothendieck category with functorial injective embeddings and bounded-below injective replacements; K^+(Inj Sh_k(X)) → D^+(Sh_k(X)) is an equivalence, and bounded derived morphisms are computed by these replacements. For a fixed finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification, D^b_S(X;k) is triangulated; cone closure also holds for two inputs sharing one such stratification.

For a finite nonempty poset of maximal strict-chain length h, a bounded finite-dimensional diagram complex in degrees [a,b] has a finite derived-limit model in [a,b+h]; complexes A,B in [a,b] and [c,d] have a finite derived-Hom model in [c−b,d−a+h]. These models commute with every field extension. Empty-poset models are zero.

Under AC, on a metric space with a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets, H^q(X,k_X) is naturally isomorphic to singular cohomology with coefficients k in every degree, also on every open subset. A nonempty contractible such space has k in degree zero and zero otherwise; this applies to finite-polyhedral open stars and their nonempty intersections with closed simplices.

seams_checked.note: Incidence F6/F7/F10/F11 preserve local constancy, metric comparison hypotheses, bar-model ranges, empty cases and AC. The injective diagram model is obtained by finite dualization over the opposite poset; descent obtains algebraic refinement from a separate supplier.

The Whitney definition preserves the analytic topology and regular-local-ring smoothness convention without claiming analytic charts from the foundation definition. The triangulation consumer uses the finite bar supplier after passing to finite-dimensional diagrams.

Analytic topology and continuity are used with separate analytification suppliers. Constant-sheaf comparison retains the metric and contractible-open-basis hypotheses; the smooth-cochain variant and filtered Godement construction are supplied locally.

The open-inclusion lemma constructs analytic manifold charts using its Jacobian and implicit-function prerequisites. The Gauss–Manin lemma explicitly supplies the integral-coefficient extension in step 1.2 rather than attributing it to the field-only comparison, and establishes its sheaf/groupoid comparison locally.
The proper-weights theorem F6 and step 2.1 construct a metric and contractible-open neighbourhood basis before applying the field-coefficient comparison. AC and naturality are retained.

Constructibility definitions are used with separate finite conical, incidence and operation suppliers. In the reverse forward-reference use, the assigned point example specializes the actual exceptional candidate to d = 0 and K = k[0]; its tensor/Hom formulas agree with the ordinary-operations supplier.

The simplicial category obtains coinduced injectives separately; fixed/common-stratification cone closure is distinguished from geometric refinement. The Stiefel comparison verifies metric manifold chart hypotheses. Uniform boundedness, finite-rank constructibility and ordinary cochain shifts are preserved.
